glosses: To incompetently perform (a task); to ruin (something) through incompetent action; to botch up, to bumble.

examples.text: I always had an idea that it would be bungled; but was willing to hope, and am still so. Whatever I can do by money, means, or person, I will venture freely for their freedom; and have so repeated to them (some of the Chiefs here) half an hour ago.

glosses: To act or work incompetently; to fumble.

examples.text: Physis is nothing else but the vegetable World, the Universall comprehension of Spermaticall life dispersed throughout. glosses: A botched or incompetently handled action or situation; a blunder.

examples.text: VVherefore this Religious affection vvhich nature has implanted, and as ſtrongly rooted in Man as the feare of death or the love of vvomen, vvould be the moſt enormous ſlip or bungle ſhe could commit, ſo that ſhe vvould ſo ſhamefully faile in the laſt Act, in this contrivance of the nature of Man, that inſtead of a Plaudite ſhe vvould deſerve to be hiſſed off the Stage.

glosses: To make a mess of; to untidy, disorder, soil, or muss.

examples.text: The afternoon breeze messed up my hair.
[…] kwatumas, those aggressive and sharp-toothed eels that so thoroughly mess up one's tackle when hooked […]

glosses: To cause a problem with; to introduce an error or mistake in; to make muddled or confused; spoil; ruin.

examples.text: The change messed something up, and it's not working anymore.

glosses: To botch, bungle; to perform poorly on.

examples.text: Well, I messed up my solo, but otherwise it was a good concert.

glosses: To make a mistake; to do something incorrectly; to perform poorly.

examples.text: She messed up on her final exam.
He has a hard time getting started because he's afraid he'll mess up.

glosses: To cause (another person) to make unwanted mistakes in a given task, usually through distraction or obnoxious behavior.

examples.text: Stop bumping me! You keep messing me up!

glosses: To damage; injure.

examples.text: He messed up his elbow at the track meet.

glosses: To manhandle; beat up; rough up.

examples.text: Her brother's friends messed him up a little after he cheated on her.

glosses: To discombobulate, utterly confuse, or confound psychologically; to throw into a state of mental disarray.

examples.text: That girl totally messed me up, man. I'm not sure who I am anymore.

glosses: Avoir la diarrhée, évacuer des excréments liquides.

examples.text: Madame Méhon en entendant cette mitraille, elle a foiré dans ses jupes.

glosses: Avoir peur, défaillir de peur, céder à un relâchement, en chier.
